DRAWN LIKE A SPORTS MANGA

Everyone here grew up on كابتن ماجد — Captain Majid. This takes the visual LANGUAGE of that 80s football-manga era: halftone screentone, converging speed lines, 3px inked panel borders, leaning impact lettering with a hard shadow behind it. Not its characters or artwork, which belong to their creators — the genre is the part people are actually nostalgic for, and it is yours to use.

Warm newsprint page, kit red, big dramatic sky, flash yellow. Every screen is live.

WHAT TO TRY

Screen 3 — "I can't make it" → "Pass my shirt on". The search is a full-bleed speed-line panel with the ball hanging in the middle of it. That is the most Tsubasa-era moment in the app, and it is pointed at the one thing CeleBreak does worst.

Screen 4 — the score lands on a sunburst. Screen 2 — the teams are inked onto a manga pitch; you are the yellow 8.

BUILT TO BE SHARED

The player card is now a character stats page — huge shirt number ghosted behind, screentone burst, stat boxes along the bottom. That is the screen people screenshot into the group chat, which is free marketing you do not have to buy.

The table gives you a gold panel when you are in the promotion places.

THE ONE RULE

Sunbursts, tilted panels and full-bleed speed lines are reserved for three beats: the goal, the win, and the money coming back.

Everywhere else the page stays flat and calm. Drama that never stops is just noise — the reason the big panels hit is that most screens do not have one.
